newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Lukashenko prepares to swoop on Belarus farmers.
newsitem.headline: Lukashenko prepares to swoop on Belarus farmers.

text.p: Belarus President Alexander Lukashenko, who has accused his country's farmers of shampooing their cows to try to impress him, will start conducting agricultural activity spot checks on Wednesday, Itar-Tass news agency said.

"Not even the personal bodyguards of the Belarussian President know the exact route the head of state will take on Wednesday to become acquainted with the situation in the depths of the countryside," the Russian agency said on Tuesday.

The hardline Lukashenko, on a discipline drive in his impoverished former Soviet republic, announced last month that he would make surprise flights over farms in his personal helicopter to ensure spring grain sowing goes to plan.
That way officials would be unable to deceive him by hastily cleaning up farms and livestock before a presidential visit.

"Tell me how you tried to pull the wool over the president's eyes and washed cows with shampoo when I was planning to visit two districts of our region," Lukashenko told the Minsk region's governor last month.

On Sunday the popular former state farm boss told his countrymen to drink less and to follow his example by taking up sport. Last week he made an example of a string of top officials of a town by sacking them all for partying at work.

Lukashenko, anxious to unite Belarus with its larger and richer neighbour Russia, has made liberals in Moscow nervous of integration by his dislike of market reform and crackdown on journalists and opposition activists.
Last week reformers in the Russian government persuaded President Boris Yeltsin to scale back a Union Treaty on building ties between the two states, although further integration is still envisaged.
